title: Lead, Program Evidence
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Head, Program Evidence, the role will lead evidence generation and use, to support Foundation’s program teams with the research and evidence needed to further Young Africa Works, EleV and other Foundation’s program objectives. The job holder will contribute to the delivery of the Program Evidence Strategy as it applies to the needs of specific program platforms. They will operationalize the delivery of strategic and demand-responsive evidence services, commission diagnostic and landscaping studies and commissioning and managing other research to enable programming. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Lead the design of research systems/processes/protocols for Program Evidence to ensure high-quality research design, implementation, and analysis. Work with the team to contribute to building a culture that encourages evidence-informed decision making. Collaborate with programs teams to identify and address research and evidence needs to enhance effectiveness of programs and partnerships and alignment to the Young Africa Works and EleV strategies. Contribute to collating, commissioning and synthesizing evidence on programmatic knowledge building including the understanding of country and regional contexts to support program co-design, implementation and review processes. Collaborate with Program teams to co-develop research partnerships aligned with programming needs and evidence development strategy. Work with the team to develop and ensure quality control of internal & externally commissioned programs research outputs and content generated. Lead the engagement with local stakeholders and program teams to determine long-term priority research needs. Write and publish learnings on the Foundations programs to influence best practice internally and externally. Disseminate relevant learnings and insights to internal and external audiences. Operationalize the delivery of Program Evidence Workplans, in alignment with the overall Functional Workplans and Goals. Work with the team to develop strong global and in-region relationships with external research and evidence partners. Work with the team to build and strengthen the capacity of others to deliver high-quality evidence, research, analysis, publications and documentation. Under the guidance of Program Evidence Heads, act as provide subject matter experts for Foundation Program Evidence work. WHO YOU ARE A Master’s or PhD in global development, the social sciences, health, eco nomics, education, public policy or another related field 7 to 10 years leadership experience in education, health, the social sciences and humanities, development and/or public policy within non-profit organizations, international NGO’s and/or learning institutions. Expertise in researching development, political, economic, cultural and social issues across Africa. Understanding of research methodologies and approaches, especially in the area of economic transformation/growth and development policy. Proven experience in effectively engaging with technical experts and institutions to build communities of practice. Experience working with and managing research or knowledge development teams with ability to plan for and prioritize multiple enterprise-wide initiatives with varying timelines. Ability to work effectively across teams and functions to achieve organizational objectives. Competencies: Technical competencies Strong research skills with the ability to translate findings to technical and non-technical teams. Experience in using research and data to design and refine programs grounded in credible, ethical, practical evidence. Demonstrated expertise in both quantitative and qualitative research or evaluation methods and tools, and ability to assess methodological rigor, blending methods, making sense of data and applying insight. Understands systems thinking and how to work towards systemic change, using multiple practices and insights including the value of foresight and trends scanning. Ability to apply ethical principles consistently throughout the research lifecycle (planning, data collection, analysis, publication). Comfortable with using techniques including but not limited to context mapping, root/deep cause analysis, and analyses through an intersectional lens. Experienced in providing guidance in the development and co-creation of research questions with programming colleagues Excellent facilitation skills Familiarity with and experience in working across Africa Other competencies (Leadership, Behavioural) Strong verbal, written, and presentation skills with the ability to articulate information to a variety of constituents across cultures. Curious and enthusiastic about pursuing new avenues of research. Open to the ideas of others and shares knowledge and insight from a place of humility. Ability to communicate effectively with and relate to a broad range of internal stakeholders including Foundation leadership. Builds and maintains strong, collaborative relationships across departments and with external stakeholders. Client service mindset, and commitment to the value of co-creation, employing deep listening and authentically inclusive approach. Energetic, independent and self-motivated individual with a solution-based approach while demonstrating innovation, integrity, quality, creativity, flexibility and resilience. Innovative and entrepreneurial individual. Fluency in languages relevant to the work; French would be desirable. The annual salary for this position is within the range of $126 000 to $156 000 (CAD) commensurate with experience, skills, and internal equity considerations. ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RECRUITMENT The Foundation uses artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled tools to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position including, but may not be limited to, the use of AI-assisted resume screening and assessments to support the initial stage of the recruitment process. Applications of qualified candidates, as identified by the AI tool, are reviewed by representatives of the Foundation before shortlisting for an interview. title: Director, Program Finance – Africa Catalytic Investment Facility
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reports to: Executive Director, Programs Finance Direct reports: Head, Finance – Africa Catalytic Investment Facility Job Purpose This role is responsible for Strategic Financial leadership and stewardship for all finance operations within the Africa Catalytic Investment Facility (“ACIF”) portfolio. The individual will be a strategic business partner and support the execution of the ACIF investment program – both in fund investments and direct investments. The role will entail review, insight and contribution to finance and tax matters of specific ACIF investments at entry, portfolio management and exit; oversight of accounting and financial reporting on the investment program to Foundation leadership; the development and refining of systems, procedures and internal processes; improving the program’s finance infrastructure and procurement; and engaging and interfacing with the Mastercard Foundation Asset Management (MFAM) team. We seek an individual with strong technical experience, as well as agility and creativity to help build and shape a relatively new platform in the Foundation. The successful individual will be a trusted advisor, business partner and thought partner to ACIF in effectively and efficiently executing its mission. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Investment Evaluation and Execution Support Serve as a finance business partner to the investment team throughout the funds and direct investment lifecycle: due diligence, transaction execution, portfolio monitoring, portfolio reporting and analytics, and exit planning. Provide an internal evaluation of direct investments and fund investments in the areas of accounting, tax, and financial reporting implications of specific investment structures, including specific jurisdictions and domiciles. Supporting fund investment, deal teams in financial analysis, particularly in evaluating fund budgets, fund models, review of fund financial statements and reporting structures, finance and reporting systems, general partner financial viability, NAV evolutions, gross to net return assumptions, and other areas of analysis. Support direct investment deal teams in financial analysis prior to third party due diligence, including reviews of potential partner financial statements, funding agreements and tax matters. Work with deal teams to identify, evaluate and engage third party financial and tax due diligence providers; review due diligence reports and support the refinement of investment theses based on their findings. Support, deal teams in identifying, drafting and assessing the execution of conditions precedent to transaction execution on the basis of third party due diligence findings. Ownership and oversight of reputational due diligence on all prospective partners, including the engagement of third party reputational due diligence providers. Review and contribute to internal investment memos from a finance, tax, accounting perspective and reputational due diligence perspective. Where possible, identify, develop and execute innovative and appropriate structures for ACIF investments to ensure compliance, risk management and financial efficiency. Identify, manage and mitigate any jurisdictional reporting, foreign exchange, capital control or other risks related to ACIF investments. Lead the oversight and execution of closing of fund and direct investments, including ensuring completion of all required internal and partner documentation, adherence to all internal governance and approval processes, overseeing internal workflows, coordinating with the team at MFAM and confirming timely execution of all procedures to fund initial and subsequent disbursements. Lead any jurisdictional / in country reporting, registering or tax related requirements to effect the execution of ACIF investments, in collaboration with third party legal, tax and finance advisors. Support portfolio companies and funds with identified gaps in the finance function, as part of the ACIF value creation strategy, strengthening the capabilities and governance of African enterprises. Platform Finance Accounting Oversight Plan, implement, manage and control all financial related internal activities within the program. Budgeting: Lead the annual budgeting process; ensure availability of sufficient funding to enable delivery of the strategic objectives as well as individual program outcomes. Lead periodic reviews of expenditures, highlight areas of concern and identify areas of savings. Act as 1st line of defence for Financial and compliance risk through identifying risks, assessing controls, and implementing mitigations against risks. Contracting and procurement management: develop, review and improve contracting to ensure value for money, efficiency and effectiveness in procurement of professional and other services. Vendor selection and negotiation: identify areas of efficiency and savings by reviewing contracts, scopes of work and vendor selection processes; engage with professional services providers for due diligence activities, negotiate terms and pricing and leveraging a holistic view of ACIF and Foundation level procurement. Liaise with internal teams, including the Global Controllers office, Shared Services, Tax and other departments to ensure awareness, compliance and reporting as needed. Oversee and implement deal profitability analysis, including identifying and sharing lessons learned. In partnership with the ACIF Senior Director, develop and improve internal templates, program policies, processes and systems to ensure the effective and efficient implementation of the program. Provide monthly financial reporting and analysis to Executive Director, Program Finance and other internal colleagues as relevant on program expenses, partner disbursements, cash flow projections, value for money, and other ad hoc reports as needed. Report status updates and provide ad-hoc support Accountable for the budgeting, planning & forecasting process within the areas of programming through the provision of accurate, timely information to enable the enterprise-wide approvals of operating plans Accountable to ensure that there are adequate internal controls are in place to mitigate the foundations against financial losses in the program Provide support to the centralized accounting function for annual audits with MFAM, independent auditors and regulatory agencies as required Embed a risk management culture within the program and ensure there are appropriate policies and other risk mitigation protocols in place together with the Senior Director, ACIF. Support the Assurance and ERM team on all matters related to auditing, assurance, compliance and risk management. Coordinate with the Canada accounting team, MFAM to assist tax and audit procedures (e.g., tax filings, year-end closing, annual audit). Investment Portfolio Reporting Create a portfolio analytics approach and reporting templates for internal and Board and Audit Committee reporting. Coordinate internal reporting to the Audit Committee, Board on the financial and accounting elements of ACIF’s investments. Lead periodic portfolio construction review, including the development of templates, internal engagement, risk management assessment and other areas to inform investment decision making and pipeline development. Coordinate the annual valuation process, in collaboration with the Investment team and MFAM. In collaboration with MFAM, coordinate any Q&A or information needs from the external auditors on specific investments. Other Be a trusted advisor, business partner and thought partner to ACIF in effectively and efficiently executing its mission. Act as a liaison with the Program Finance team and Executive Director, Program Finance to ensure awareness, input and regular insight into ACIF investments and other activities. Act as a collaborative cross-functional leader within the organization, bringing best practice to ACIF drawing on insights from program finance colleagues in other areas of the enterprise. In collaboration with the ACIF legal business partner, maintain delegation of authority procedures and other compliance internal related functions Participate in all ACIF team meetings, internal workshops, etc to provide perspective, inputs, guidance. Participate in all ACIF ExCo screenings, Investment Advisory Committee meetings and other leadership engagements. Ensure ACIF is consistently aware of Foundation best practices, policies, procedures and adheres to the highest standard of corporate governance and risk mitigation. WHO YOU ARE Bachelor’s degree in Business (Commerce, Business Administration, Management) or related field; MBA or relevant Master’s degree added advantage Relevant professional qualification; CPA, CA and Member of a relevant professional body. Minimum 15 years in progressively senior financial roles within an investment institution or a Big Four audit firm with a focus on financial due diligence and private equity in African jurisdictions, with at least 7 years in a management capacity. Experience managing and building capabilities and capacity of accounting and operations teams in high growth organizations including supporting expansion in multi-jurisdictional and multi-currency environments. Experience in supporting private equity funds, either from a fund of funds lens or a direct investing lens (ideally both) – as an internal finance professional or a finance due diligence advisor. Experience building reporting frameworks, templates and analytics. Familiarity and experience with SPVs, holding companies, fund structures, fund an investment valuation, investment accounting, IFRS and GAAP reporting; experience with charity accounting a plus. Senior leadership experience obtained across multiple territories. Competencies: Technical competencies Working Knowledge: Operate Accounting Systems, Generate Routine Accounting Records and Financial Reports Working Knowledge: Determine and apply correct accounting treatments; Able to Identify & Mitigate Operational, Financial and Business Risks; Manage Operational Internal Control Systems, Processes, and Policies; Financial Processes & Accounting Operations Management Expertise in Analytics of Financial and Non-Financial Information to generate insights for decision support. Interpretation of Financial Information and Generating Insights for decision support. Excellent management & Financial Reporting including Financial Forecasting & Budgeting. Other competencies (Leadership, Behavioural ) Demonstrated initiative and drive towards innovative problem solving Honed business partnership skills with Impeccable integrity Ability to assess risks and exercise judgment in making important decisions. Ability to challenge and provide feedback in a constructive manner with the goal of improving efficiency and operational excellence Flexible, adaptable, and able to execute a range of job duties and changing priorities. Possess excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills with the ability to articulate information to a variety of constituents across cultures. Possess professional maturity, sensitivity with different cultures, and impeccable integrity. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. title: Lead, Fellows, Canada Programs
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Work-Model : Hybrid Employment Type : Full-Time Role type : Existing Position Reporting to the Head, Indigenous Youth Leadership Program, The Lead, Fellows Program is responsible for leading the successful implementation, growth, and continuous improvement of the Mastercard Foundation Fellows Program. Reporting to the Head, Indigenous Youth Leadership Program, the role oversees a portfolio of host organization partnerships that support Fellows across Canada. The Lead works closely with partners to ensure high-quality program delivery, meaningful youth experiences, and strong outcomes for Fellows and their communities. The role is responsible for developing and deepening partnerships, advancing Indigenous approaches to program learning and impact measurement, elevating Fellows stories and leadership, and identifying opportunities to expand the programs reach and influence. The Lead, Fellows Program collaborates across Foundation teams and with external stakeholders to ensure that Indigenous youth voices remain at the center of program implementation, learning, and growth. Due to the nature of this position, which requires direct engagement with Indigenous communities, preference will be given to qualified Indigenous candidates. Applicants who wish to qualify for preferential consideration are encouraged to self-identify in their applications and will be required to provide reasonable confirmation of Indigenous identity. Indigenous candidates are encouraged to self-identify and apply even if they do not meet all components listed. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Partnership Relations Lead relationship management and performance oversight for a portfolio of Fellows Program host organization partners across Canada. Support host partners in delivering high-quality programming that aligns with the goals, principles, and outcomes of the Mastercard Foundation Fellows Program. Lead planning, implementation, problem-solving, and adaptive management with partners, identifying risks and opportunities and escalating issues as required. Monitor partner performance and progress against agreed objectives, budgets, learning commitments, and reporting requirements. Identify and cultivate strategic partnerships that support the growth and long-term sustainability of the Mastercard Foundation Fellows Program. Develop and maintain relationships with Indigenous and non-Indigenous leaders, organizations, institutions, and networks to create opportunities for Fellows. Serve as a connector across the Indigenous youth leadership ecosystem, strengthening relationships among Fellows, partners, institutions, communities, and Foundation networks. Program Management Support contracting, grant management, budgeting, reporting, and compliance processes related to Fellows Program partnerships. Coordinate annual program planning processes and support the implementation of program workplans, collaborating with host partners and internal Foundation staff. Collaborate closely with Foundation colleagues across Canada Programs, Finance, Legal, Communications, Impact, and other functions to support effective program delivery. Lead planning and coordination of Fellow convenings, gatherings, engagement opportunities, and other program activities. Contribute to recommendations regarding program growth, innovation, and future strategic direction for Foundation executive. Program Learning, Impact & Continuous Improvement Support the development and implementation of an Indigenous evaluation and impact framework for the Mastercard Foundation Fellows Program. Analyze program reports, data, and emerging insights to identify opportunities for continuous improvement. Contribute to the development of internal reporting, briefings, learning products, and decision-making materials. Support the identification and amplification of Fellows stories, accomplishments, and leadership journeys. Collaborate with colleagues across Foundation teams to share implementation learnings, strengthen program delivery, and identify opportunities for collaboration. Represent the Fellows Program in external learning events and internal communities of practice, working groups, and cross-functional initiatives related to youth engagement, leadership development, Indigenous programming, and partnership management. Contribute to Foundation learning and thought leadership on Indigenous youth leadership, Indigenous ways of knowing, and youth engagement. Perform additional responsibilities and special projects as assigned. WHO YOU ARE Academic and Professional Qualifications Undergraduate degree in Indigenous Studies, Education, Community Development, Social Sciences, Public Policy, Business Administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, lived experience, and relevant professional experience. Demonstrated understanding of Indigenous worldviews, leadership approaches, and community development practices. Graduate degrees are considered an asset. Training or certification in project management, partnership development, evaluation, or related disciplines is considered an asset. Experience Minimum five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in Indigenous education, youth leadership, youth development, employment, community development, or related fields. Demonstrated experience working with Indigenous communities, Nations, organizations, and youth across Canada. Experience developing and managing strategic, complex partnerships, networks, and stakeholder relationships. Experience leading or supporting the implementation of large-scale programs involving multiple partners and workstreams. Experience supporting program evaluation, learning, impact measurement, or research initiatives. Experience working with fellowships, scholarships, youth leadership, or leadership development programs is considered a strong asset. Experience applying Indigenous ways of knowing and being is considered a strong asset. Technical Competencies Strong partnership management and stakeholder engagement skills. Strong program and project management capabilities. Excellent verbal, written, facilitation, and presentation skills. Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Ability to synthesize complex information and communicate insights effectively to diverse audiences. Strong planning, coordination, and organizational skills. Knowledge of Indigenous youth leadership, education, and community development ecosystems across Canada. Understanding of Indigenous approaches to evaluation, learning, and community engagement. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams). Leadership and Behavioral Competencies Lived experience as an Indigenous person in Canada is strongly preferred. Deep commitment to Indigenous youth leadership, self-determination, and community well-being. Excellent relationship-building and interpersonal skills. Demonstrates humility, cultural awareness, active listening, and respect in all interactions. Highly organized with strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities. Self-motivated and able to work independently while contributing effectively to a team environment. Flexible and adaptable, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and evolving priorities. Commitment to continuous learning, reflection, and improvement. Alignment with the Foundations values and mission. The annual salary for this position is within the range of $125 000 to $140 000 (CAD) commensurate with experience, skills, and internal equity considerations. title: Lead, Agrifoods Systems - WAEMU
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Director, Entrepreneurship Development, the Lead, Agrifoods Systems will support the building of impactful country programs by setting direction and engaging partners throughout program design and implementation of the WAEMU Roadmap, WAEMU One Plan & Agrifood priorities within the WAEMU Roadmap. S/he will provide expertise to identify constraints that prevent agrifoods systems from functioning effectively at the country level and incorporating the agricultural sector’s needs into country strategies. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Provide agricultural sector expertise to support the Foundation country teams in the design and management of agricultural and Agri-finance programs. Identify challenges and opportunities in the agri-food systems to drive job growth. Collaborate with country teams and other team members in the development or implementation of new programs, including co-creation of programs and due diligence practices. Communicate progress and learnings from projects to the Foundation colleagues and the wider development community. Collaborate with the program and country teams to leverage synergies across programs, platforms and across geographies. Manage current programs, distilling learnings for the Foundation staff and country teams. Provide perspective and expertise on emerging issues and trends in the agricultural and Agri-finance sector, including climate change. Contribute insights to the Foundation’s thought leadership on youth employment in Africa. Lead and supervise teams of colleagues and/or junior experts by providing coaching and support necessary for success and growth. Identify and help overcome challenges and other barriers to team effectiveness. Build relationships with partner organizations, communities of practice, and global stakeholders. Represent the Foundation and collaborate with key internal and external audiences. WHO YOU ARE Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Finance, Business, Agricultural Economics and/or Financial Inclusion. Minimum ten (10) years of relevant experience in financing agricultural companies and farmers is required. Minimum 5 years of leadership and management experience. Excellent project management skills, including multi-stakeholder projects. Experience working in commercial agricultural companies operational in Africa, West Africa, or WAEMU. Demonstrates a strong understanding of the role of financial inclusion in economic growth and development, particularly in Africa, and as it relates to smallholder farmers. Understands market and systemic challenges to financial inclusion for rural and agricultural economics in Africa and best practices for addressing them. Experience and understanding in a variety of value chains (cash and food crops), the small businesses and SMEs along the value chain, and supply chain / logistics in the agri-food system. Understanding of the role of agri-food and rural SMEs in economic transformation and job creation for youth. Demonstrates a strong understanding of agricultural markets in Africa and the systemic challenges leading to stagnant growth. Demonstrates strong analytical skills, the ability to think strategically and contribute as a thought partner in the Foundation’s strategy development. Demonstrates strong budgeting skills with the ability to manage a large portfolio of assets. Command of quantitative and qualitative business analytics. Flexible, adaptable, and able to execute a range of job duties and changing priorities. Proven excellence in verbal, written, and presentation skills with the ability to articulate information to a variety of constituents across cultures and to distill complex information and data into accessible conversation and written pieces. Possess professional maturity, sensitivity with different cultures, and impeccable integrity that exemplify the Foundation’s values. You have a commitment to Mastercard Foundation’s values and vision. title: Partner, Partner Engagement
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Head, Partner Stewardship, the Partner will support the design, coordination, and execution of a comprehensive Partner Stewardship and Accompaniment Framework across the Foundations portfolio. The role will serve as a key operational driver within the Partner Stewardship team, working across the pillars of the Partner Engagement Framework. The Partner will play a critical role in translating the Partner Stewardship strategy into practical, day-to-day delivery; coordinating accompaniment activities, supporting the design and rollout of partner engagement initiatives, and ensuring consistency and quality across all partner touchpoints. The role will work closely with internal teams, including Program Teams (Countries & other Platforms), Impact, Evidence & Learning, Strategic Insights & Program Performance, Programming Excellence, and external stakeholders including the Foundation Partners and accompaniment/institutional strengthening partners. THE ROLE Partner Accompaniment Coordination Support the design and rollout of Partner Accompaniment, including the Partner opt-in and onboarding process, Partner capacity assessments, and Capacity Action Plans (CAPs). Coordinate the delivery of accompaniment activities across Partner archetypes, regions, and themes, ensuring alignment with the Foundation’s accompaniment principles and values. Maintain and regularly update the Marketplace Directory of vetted capacity accompaniment providers available to Partner Coordinate the provision, monitoring and tracking of all capacity enhancement activities by various teams at the Foundation, ensuring all providers are aligned with the Foundation’s engagement and accompaniment framework. Partner Experience and Engagement Support the standardization of partner onboarding, engagement, and feedback processes to ensure a consistent and positive partner experience across the portfolio. Support the bi-annual Partner survey, coordinating data collection, analyzing feedback, and tracking the implementation of recommended actions. Monitor and help address partner experience incidents, escalating to the Head as required, and documenting learnings for continuous improvement. Maintain open communication with partners and support the gathering of feedback to build trust and improve partner experience over time. Frameworks, Tools, and Systems Support the development and maintenance of guidelines, frameworks, tools, and processes that underpin Partner Stewardship and Accompaniment, including the Partner Resource Hub, Partner Connect, and other digital engagement on the Daraja Platform. Research and implement lean, smart, and agile processes to enhance clarity, efficiency, and creativity in partner stewardship and accompaniment delivery. Track, document, and leverage learnings to improve partner engagement, support allocation, and program outcomes on an ongoing basis. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Support the monitoring and tracking of partner accompaniment outcomes across the portfolio, contributing to regular reporting to Foundation leadership. Support evidence generation, documentation of key learnings, and translation of insights into adaptive improvements to the accompaniment and overall Partner stewardship model. Promote a collaborative environment for partners to share knowledge, resources, and experiences to address common challenges and leverage learnings for improved performance Internal Capability and Coordination Support the building of partner stewardship capabilities of Foundation staff, ensuring engagement is consistent and responsive to evolving partner needs. Coordinate cross-functional engagement with Program Teams, Impact, legal, Finance, Program Performance, and other enabling functions to ensure coherence in partner stewardship delivery. Contribute to the positioning of the Foundation as a thought leader in partner engagement and accompaniment by supporting development of knowledge products, knowledge sharing and institutional relationship management. WHO YOU ARE University degree in development studies, business administration, social sciences, or a related field is required. Relevant certification in program management, organizational development is an advantage Minimum of Five (5) years of relevant experience in partner management, organisational development, capacity strengthening, or programme management, with demonstrated progression into roles of increasing complexity and responsibility. Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing capacity strengthening or accompaniment programmes across diverse organisational types including non-profit, private sector, academic, and public institutions. Experience working with and across African organisations and contexts, with a strong understanding of the diversity of the African development ecosystem. Experience in partnership management, process design, and stakeholder engagement across complex, multi-stakeholder environments. Familiarity with monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks and their application in partner accompaniment or programme quality contexts. Experience working across multiple geographies and cultural contexts, with the ability to adapt approaches to different organisational and regional realities – Added advantage. Competencies: Highly organised with strong coordination and project management skills; able to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously without losing attention to detail. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; able to translate data and partner feedback into actionable improvements. Skilled communicator and influencer: Able to engage confidently at all levels, from Foundation leadership and senior external stakeholders to Partners and Accompaniment Partners on the ground. Equally comfortable producing clear written communications, facilitating complex conversations, and navigating sensitive situations with discretion and professionalism. Critical thinker with an agile mindset; comfortable navigating ambiguity and responding to change with professionalism. Strong partnership mindset; able to build trusted relationships with partners and align stakeholders across different roles toward common goals. Familiarity with Foundation processes and policies yet unafraid to innovate and improve them. Skilled at cross-functional coordination and collaboration across technical and operational teams. Results-driven with a pragmatic approach to decision-making and a strong eye for detail. Experience working in complex, fast-moving environments with multiple internal and external stakeholders. Influencing without authority that enables coordination across Accompaniment Partners, internal Foundation teams, and other stakeholders without direct line authority over any of them. Comfort with ambiguity and adaptive management Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite and digital collaboration platforms. Possess professional maturity, sensitivity with different cultures, and impeccable integrity that exemplify the Foundation’s values Demonstrate a commitment to Mastercard Foundation’s values and vision. title: Lead, Programming Excellence
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Head, Programming Excellence, the role will lead and coordinate programming excellence across programs. The role will be responsible for driving efficiencies, effectiveness, and quality assurance of overall end-to-end programming processes and partner experience. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Lead Foundation-wide programming processes, standards and capacity building strategies Coordinate with the various delivery platforms to support consistent quality in scaling of the Foundation’s programs to help generate dignified work for more young people. Oversee program management and implementation processes, policies, and guidelines (work in coordination/consultation with enabling functions to ensure enterprise cohesion) Manage the program implementation processes, policies, guidelines and standards ensuring quality, coherence and alignment of all program processes post final design and enhancement of IPIA to Programming for Impact Take ownership of guidelines, tools, processes, templates to ensure standardization in coordination and consultation with OE. Enhance & streamline programming processes, workflows, documents, tools and overall process turnaround time for positive partner experience Work with Program Finance to measure, monitor & track program processes for effectiveness and efficiencies Implement recommendations to enhance program processes Manage and govern revisions to all programmatic processes, policies, guidelines in coordination with core relevant cross functional departments. Monitor the implementation of program-wide processes, policies, guidelines and standards and d lead the development and implementation of changes to ensure continued coherence and alignment to the evolving programming needs. Identify and curate contents for the Program Academy to drive capability, effective onboard and learning within Programs Team Drive capability enhancement across Program teams through trainings, workshops & learning within the Program teams in coordination with P&C & Foundation Academy Work with P&C to embed program learning in programming processes WHO YOU ARE University degree, preferably in business administration or a related field is required; Masters Degree will be advantageous. Program Management experience Minimum of Ten (10) years of experience driving program delivery Two (2) years leadership and management experience in a multi-country environment in Africa, with a preference for private sector experience. Experience in partnership management, process design & program management within nonprofit organizations, international NGO’s and/or learning institutions is also helpful. Competencies: Mastery of Microsoft Office suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel). Strong coordination, project planning and program management skills. Advanced skills in process mapping and management Excellent organizational and prioritization skills; demonstrated attention to detail and ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously. Exposure to strategic systems thinking with an ability to understand and engage with stakeholders in different ecosystems and design programming that addresses root causes and critical needs.
